name: get_accounts
title: Get Accounts
description:
List customer's PAID trading accounts (CFD + Futures + legacy Stellar/Evaluation/Express). The primary 'show my accounts' tool.

WHEN TO USE:
- 'my accounts', 'show accounts', 'active accounts', 'inactive accounts', 'breached accounts'
- Account search by login number
- Account filter by plan family (Stellar/Eval/Express)

WHEN NOT TO USE — route to the SPECIFIC sibling:
- 'free trial accounts' / 'trial accounts' → use get_free_trial_accounts instead
- 'competition accounts' / 'free competition' / 'giveaway accounts' → use get_free_competition_accounts instead
- Single account drill-down (balance, equity, drawdown, objectives) → use get_account_overview instead
- Plan/platform/subscription dates for one account → use get_account_plan_info instead

CALLING PATTERN: For 'my accounts' with no specifier, customer typically has BOTH CFD and Futures. Call twice in parallel: (type=active, tab=forex) and (type=active, tab=futures), then merge.

FAILURE ANALYSIS PATTERN ('I failed X times — what's common cause?'):
1. Call get_accounts(type='breached', tab='forex') + get_accounts(type='breached', tab='futures') in parallel
2. List all breached accounts to customer with login + plan name
3. Call get_rule_breach_history for each → find common breach_reason
4. Cross-reference with get_cycle_overview on active accounts to find bad (negative P&L) cycles too

PREREQUISITES: none — only the customer's auth token. No account_id needed; this tool is how you DISCOVER account ids (and logins) for every other account tool. When a customer names a login but you need the internal account_id, you can also call resolve_account(login).

RETURNS: Array of accounts. Each has:
- id: internal account_id (use with other tools)
- login: customer-visible MT5/cTrader/Tradovate login
- plan: plan name
- balance, equity: current values
- status: 'active' | 'inactive' | 'breached'
- category_id: 1=CFD, 2=Futures
- server.server_type: 'mt4' | 'mt5' | 'ctrader' | 'matchtrader' | 'tradovate'
- breached: 0=active, 1=breached
Response is paginated (current_page/last_page/per_page/total) — page through it for aggregation questions.

ERROR HANDLING:
- 422 'tab must be forex or futures' → never send 'cfd', use 'forex'
- 401 → auth token missing/expired; customer must re-authenticate
- Empty array → no accounts of that type/status (not an error; tell customer plainly)

FOLLOW-UP: After listing, customer often wants a specific account's details → get_account_overview using account_id from this response.

type.description: Account STATUS filter (REQUIRED). MUST be exactly one of: 'active', 'inactive', 'breached'. This is a STATUS, NOT an account category — do NOT pass 'all', 'paid', 'funded', 'challenge', 'cfd', 'forex' or any other value (they fail validation). To filter by CFD vs Futures use the `tab` param; to filter by package use `plan`. For a plain 'show my accounts', default to 'active'. Meanings: 'active' = currently tradeable (passed challenge, not breached, not expired). 'inactive' = expired subscription, not-yet-funded, or dormant. name: get_account_overview
title: Get Account Overview
description:
Get detailed metrics for ONE trading account: balance, equity, drawdown, cycle info, plan details, breach info, objectives (DLL/MLL/PT/MTD/CR), risk parameter summary.

WHEN TO USE: Customer asks about a specific account's state — 'how is my account doing', 'account status', 'balance', 'my drawdown', 'profit target progress', 'how much can I lose before breach', 'am I on track to pass'.

WHEN NOT TO USE — route to the SPECIFIC sibling:
- Listing multiple accounts → use get_accounts instead
- Trade-level data (individual closed/open trades) → use get_trading_history instead
- Plan name / platform / subscription end date / cycle dates only → use get_account_plan_info instead
- Per-cycle risk verdict drill-down on a funded account → use get_risk_card + get_risk_parameters instead
- Why a breached account failed (triggering trades) → use get_rule_breach_history instead

PREREQUISITES:
- Need account_id (internal). If customer gives login number, call resolve_account(login) first. If no account context at all, call get_accounts first to discover ids.

AMBIGUOUS 'MY ACCOUNT' RESOLUTION: If customer says 'my account' (singular, no specifier) and has multiple active accounts:
1. Pick the MOST RECENTLY ACTIVE account (most recent trade time, fall back to most recent login)
2. State the choice explicitly: 'Pulling your most recent account — login 12345, Stellar 2-Step 50K. Tell me if you meant a different one.'
3. Customer can then redirect.

RETURNS: objectives block (DLL/MLL/PT/MTD/CR each with target_value, current_value, status), account_details block (login, initial_balance, breached, breached_by, server, payout_eligibility, account_growth), trading_cycle_details block (starting_date, ending_date, payout_eligible_date).

RISK BUFFER ("how much can I lose before breach?") — answer directly from:
- objectives.daily_loss.daily_loss_till_now: remaining DAILY loss allowance in DOLLARS
- objectives.overall_loss.max_loss_till_now: remaining OVERALL loss allowance in DOLLARS
- target_value_percentage on each gives the limit as % of initial balance
Quote these verbatim. Do NOT recompute buffer from balance yourself.

PAYOUT ETA ("when will I get paid?", "next payout date") — use trading_cycle_details.payout_eligible_date (ISO date, or 'N/A' if not applicable). Pair with search_knowledge for processing-time policy.

PASS PROGRESS ("am I on track to pass?") — for EACH visible objective report current_value / target_value + status as a checklist: profit (PT), daily_loss (DLL), overall_loss (MLL), trading_days (MTD). status integers: 1=PASSED, 2=ON_GOING. quick_strike block (when present) has violation_percentage + is_violated.

TRADING DAYS REQUIREMENT: objectives.trading_days block contains:
- target_value: plan's MINIMUM required trading days (challenge accounts only — EV/EX plan types)
- current_value: actual trading days so far this cycle
- status: PASSED or ON_GOING
USE FOR: 'how many trading days do I need?', 'am I meeting trading day requirement?', 'will I pass?'

ERROR HANDLING:
- 404 → account_id not owned by customer or doesn't exist. Re-list via get_accounts.
- 401 → auth expired; customer must re-authenticate.
- Breached account → response includes breach_reason; surface to customer (and offer get_rule_breach_history for full detail).

name: get_rule_breach_history
title: Get Rule Breach History
description:
Full breach explanation for one account: which rule triggered, when, trades at breach time, drawdown metrics.

WHEN TO USE: Any 'why was I breached', 'breach reason', 'what happened', 'what rule did I break', 'show me the trades that caused the breach'. Also useful for forfeited accounts.

WHEN NOT TO USE — route to the SPECIFIC sibling:
- Non-breached account → returns empty/null; use get_account_overview instead
- Risk/Margin verdict on a funded (Real) account → use get_risk_card + get_risk_parameters instead
- A negative-P&L cycle on a funded account that did NOT breach → use get_cycle_overview instead (see distinction below)

ACCOUNT RESOLUTION — NEVER ask customer for account ID:
1. No account context → call get_accounts(type='breached') to list all failed accounts
2. Customer mentions login → call resolve_account(login) → use returned id

MULTI-ACCOUNT FAILURE PATTERN ('I failed 3 times — what's common cause?'):
1. Call get_accounts(type='breached', tab='forex') AND get_accounts(type='breached', tab='futures') in parallel
2. Collect all breached account IDs
3. Call get_rule_breach_history for EACH in parallel
4. Group by breach_reason → find the most common rule
5. Synthesize: 'All 3 of your failed accounts were breached by DLL — you hit the daily loss limit each time'

CYCLE VS BREACH DISTINCTION — important:
- 'Failed' on a CHALLENGE account (Evaluation/Express/Stellar challenge phase) = account breached → use this tool
- 'Failed' on a FUNDED account = could mean negative P&L cycle (not a breach) → use get_cycle_overview instead
- Funded account WITH a breach → also use this tool

PREREQUISITES: account id (the {id} path param — same as account_id from get_accounts response). Resolve via resolve_account(login) or get_accounts(type='breached').

RETURNS: breach_reason (DLL/MLL/CR/Forfeit/etc.), breach_time, trades at breach time (ticket/symbol/profit/lots), metrics (maxDailyLoss/maxMonthlyLoss/maxLossLimit, balance/equity during breach).

INTERPRETATION:
- DLL = Daily Loss Limit hit (lost too much in one day)
- MLL = Max Loss Limit hit (total drawdown exceeded)
- CR = Consistency Rule violation
- Real account field: 'maxLossLimit'; Demo: 'maxMonthlyLoss'
- MT4/MT5 lots formatted differently from cTrader/Tradovate

ERROR HANDLING:
- 404 → account not owned by customer; re-list via get_accounts
- 401 → auth expired; customer must re-authenticate
- Empty/null → account was not breached; switch to get_account_overview

CUSTOMER RESPONSE FORMAT — empathetic, plain language:
- 'Your account was breached on [date formatted human-friendly]'
- Translate breach_reason: DLL → 'daily loss limit', MLL → 'maximum loss limit (overall drawdown)', CR → 'consistency rule', Forfeit → 'account forfeited'
- 'The rule that caught you: you hit your daily loss limit. This means you lost more than your plan allows in a single trading day.'
- Show the triggering trades in plain language: '[Symbol] [BUY/SELL] — lost $X at [time]'
- 'On that day your balance dropped from $X to $Y, crossing below your $Z daily limit'
- End with empathy + next step: 'This is a very common reason traders don't pass — here is what to watch for next time: ...'
- NEVER use field names like 'maxDailyLoss', 'breach_reason', 'DLL' — always translate

TERM TRANSLATIONS:
- DLL → 'Daily Loss Limit' → 'you lost too much in a single day'
- MLL / maxLossLimit → 'Maximum Loss Limit' → 'your total drawdown exceeded the allowed maximum'
- CR → 'Consistency Rule' → 'your profits were too concentrated in single days'
- Forfeit → 'the account was forfeited (admin action)'
FOLLOW-UP: Customer wants to retry → reset_eligibility_check / get_reset_eligible_accounts.

description:

WHEN TO USE:
- 'What's my W9 status?', 'Is my tax form approved?', 'Did my W9 go through?', 'tax form status', 'have I submitted my W9?'

- Customer wants year-end income documents (the downloadable 1099-NEC PDFs) -> use get_1099_info instead.
- Customer is NOT a US resident -> do not call; explain W-9/W-8 tax forms apply only to customers FundedNext must report to under US tax rules. Confirm residency with get_profile (country) when unsure, since a non-USA customer here returns 400.

PREREQUISITES: Authenticated customer; their account country must be United States. No parameters. If you are unsure of the customer's country, call get_profile first.

RETURNS: { submitted: boolean, status: string }. status is one of: 'Not Submitted' | 'Pending' | 'Rejected' | 'Approved'. submitted is false only when status is 'Not Submitted'. (Status is re-synced from Avalara on each call for non-approved records, so it reflects the latest review state.)

- Not Submitted (submitted=false) -> customer has not completed a form yet; route them to request_w9_form + the dashboard 'Tax Documents' page.

- Rejected -> form was declined (e.g. TIN mismatch); customer must resubmit via request_w9_form + dashboard.
- Approved -> tax form on file and valid; customer is clear to withdraw.

- 400 'W9 form is only available for USA customers' -> the customer's country is not United States. Do not retry; explain the form does not apply to them.
- 401 -> auth/session expired; customer must re-authenticate.
- 500 -> transient backend/Avalara error; retry once, then offer human support. Do NOT tell the customer they are 'Not Submitted' on a 500 — that is an error, not a status.

Returns the customer's REDEMPTION history — every time they spent Infinity Points for a reward coupon, including the coupon code, validity, points spent, and whether the coupon was used on an order.

WHEN TO USE: 'redeem history', 'past redemptions', 'my coupons from points', 'what have I unlocked', 'show me the coupon I redeemed'.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Task submission history (EARNING points) → use get_task_activity_history instead.
- Rewards still available to redeem → use get_redeems instead.

PREREQUISITES: Authenticated customer session. Optional limit / sort.

RETURNS: Laravel-paginated → { data: [ ...redemptions ], current_page, last_page, per_page, total }. Each row is the raw infinity_task_redeem_submissions record with coupon and redeem relations, plus a hasCouponOrder field (the created_at of a completed order that used this coupon, or null if unused). Quote values verbatim; do NOT invent fields. Key fields include: id, redeem_id, coupon_id, coupon_code, validity_time (coupon expiry), redeem_amount (points spent), remarks, created_at.

ERROR HANDLING:
- 404 'Invalid customer requested!' → customer record not found; escalate.
- 401 → re-authenticate.
- 500 → transient; retry once then escalate.

name: get_account_all_cycles_summary
title: All-Cycle Account Summary
description:
Lifetime, ALL-CYCLE summary for ONE trading account in a single call: per-cycle metrics for EVERY subscription cycle (not just the current one) plus account-level lifetime totals.

WHEN TO USE — any all-time / cross-cycle question:
- 'What is my all-time win rate / profit factor on this account?'
- 'Compare all my cycles — which was best and worst?'
- 'How much have I made across every reset on this account?'
- 'How many times have I passed then breached?'

WHEN NOT TO USE — for the CURRENT cycle only, use get_cycle_overview / get_trading_overview; for one specific past cycle use get_cycle_overview with that cycle_id.

WHY THIS EXISTS: get_cycle_overview and get_trading_overview are locked to the current subscription and silently hide prior-cycle history. This tool removes the N-call fan-out for heavy accounts (some have 90+ cycles).

P&L NOTE: all profit/loss is TRADE-TRUTHFUL — net of commission and swap, computed from the actual closed trades in each cycle (not from daily balance snapshots), so it is correct even for accounts that reset several times in one day. net_profit_loss_pct is relative to the plan starting balance.

PREREQUISITES: account_id. If the customer gives a login number, call resolve_account first.

RETURNS: { account{ id, login, plan, platform(cfd|futures), starting_balance, is_breached }, totals{ cycle_count, lifetime_net_profit_loss, all_time_win_rate, all_time_profit_factor, total_trades, passes, breaches, best_cycle{cycle_number,net_profit_loss}, worst_cycle{...} }, cycles[ per-cycle { cycle_number, label, start, end, is_current, ended_reason(running|payout_reset|breach), starting_balance, net_profit_loss, net_profit_loss_pct, trade_count, win_rate, profit_factor, gross_profit, gross_loss, best_trade, worst_trade, trading_days, total_commission, total_swap } ] }. Cycles are oldest-first.

Which special rules / add-ons apply to ONE account (daily loss limit, max loss, profit target, news-trading allowed, no-consistency-rule, min-trading-days, etc.) and whether each is a per-account override vs plan default. Existing tools only return a flat addon string + core objectives.

name: get_account_breach_events_full
title: Full Account Breach History
description:
FULL per-account breach history for ONE trading account — EVERY breach event ever recorded, newest first, PAGINATED — plus an account-wide cause breakdown. Not just the latest breach.

WHEN TO USE — any 'all my breaches' / 'why did I keep failing' question:
- 'Show me ALL the times this account was breached'
- 'List every rule breach on this account'
- 'What was the common cause across my failures?'
- 'How many times has this account been breached, and when?'

WHEN NOT TO USE — for only the single most-recent breach, the dashboard's standard breach view already covers it; for live consistency-rule standing use get_account_consistency_status; for free-trial breaches use get_free_trial_breach_history.

WHY THIS EXISTS: the standard breach view exposes only the SINGLE latest breach event (hasOne latest). This tool returns the complete list so the full failure history and the most common cause are answerable in one call. Heavy accounts can have thousands of events, so the list is always paginated (default 20, max 50 per page) and the cause breakdown / date range are computed across ALL events.

READING THE ANSWER: summary.reason_breakdown is sorted most-common-first; summary.most_common_reason answers 'what was the common cause'. summary.total_breach_events is the full count across all pages. Each data[] row carries breach_reason, balance_at_breach / equity_at_breach (verbatim), a metrics snapshot of the rule thresholds at breach time, the owning subscription cycle, and created_at. Internal/admin ops notes are returned as neutral customer-safe wording with is_internal_note=true; quote those rows as a team action, never as a specific rule breach.

PREREQUISITES: account_id. If the customer gives a login number, call resolve_account first.

RETURNS: { current_page, per_page, total, last_page, from, to, data[ { id, login, breach_reason, is_internal_note, balance_at_breach, equity_at_breach, metrics{ maxDailyLoss, maxMonthlyLoss|maxLossLimit, lastDayBalance, lastDayEquity, balanceDuringBreachTime, equityDuringBreachTime, metricDate } | null, cycle{ cycle_id, cycle_number, label } | null, created_at } ], account{ id, login, is_breached }, summary{ total_breach_events, first_breach_at, last_breach_at, most_common_reason, reason_breakdown[ { breach_reason, count } ] } }. Events are newest-first.

name: get_certificate_display_name
title: Certificate Display Name
description:
The name currently set to PRINT on the customer's certificates. Existing certificate tools only return a boolean flag for whether a name is set; this returns the actual value.

WHEN TO USE: 'what name will be on my certificate', 'is my certificate showing the right name', 'did I set a custom certificate name'.

PREREQUISITES: none — scoped to the authenticated customer.

RETURNS: { has_custom_name (bool), certificate_name (string|null), message }.

name: get_certificate_period_stats
title: Certificate Period Stats
description:
Per-certificate trading stats scoped to the certificate's OWN subscription cycle — the exact account state and trading performance from WHEN the certificate was earned, NOT the account's current cycle.

WHEN TO USE:
- 'What were my stats when I earned this certificate?'
- 'Show the balance / equity curve for this certificate's actual period.'
- 'What was my profit / win rate / drawdown on the cycle that won me this certificate?'

WHY THIS EXISTS: get_cycle_overview / get_trading_overview are locked to the CURRENT subscription, so once an account resets after a payout the trading numbers behind an older certificate disappear. Each certificate already records the subscription_id it was earned under, so this tool pins the standard cycle overview to that historical window and returns the historically-correct numbers.

IDENTIFYING THE CERTIFICATE: pass doc_id (the certificate's id, as returned by get_account_certificates / get_all_customer_certificates) and/or login. At least ONE is required. When only login is given, the most-recent certificate on that account is used. If the customer gives a login number, you may pass it directly here.

P&L NOTE: balance/equity curve, drawdown, daily-loss and balance stats come from the daily account_metrics snapshots for the certificate's subscription window; win-rate, profit factor, gross profit/loss and best/worst trade come from the actual closed trades in that window.

RETURNS: { certificate{ doc_id, certificate_id, name, reference, account_id, login, subscription_id, issued_at, url }, period{ id, cycle_number, label, start, end, is_current, ended_reason }, overview{ start_balance, end_balance, peak_balance, lowest_balance, peak_equity, profit_loss, profit_loss_pct, gross_profit, gross_loss, max_daily_loss_hit, max_drawdown_pct, total_trading_days, total_trades, win_rate, profit_factor, avg_winning_trade, avg_losing_trade, best_trade, worst_trade, total_commission, total_swap }, balance_curve[ { date, balance, equity } ] }. period/overview are null when the certificate is not linked to a specific subscription cycle (legacy certificates).

doc_id.description: The certificate's id (account_certificates id) as returned by get_account_certificates / get_all_customer_certificates. Resolves a single specific certificate.

login.description: The MT login number of the account. When supplied without doc_id, the most-recent certificate earned on that account is used.

name: get_competition_my_result
title: My Competition Result
description:
The authenticated customer's OWN final result in ONE competition: did they win, their finishing position, gain %, prize, package, winner type (General vs Lottery), certificate status, and disbursement status — or won:false if they have no winner row.

WHEN TO USE — questions about the customer's OWN outcome in a specific competition:
- 'Did I win the competition?' / 'Did I win the lottery?'
- 'What position did I finish and what prize did I win?'
- 'Is my competition certificate ready?'
- 'Did I get my competition payout / prize disbursed?'

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- The PUBLIC list of all winners / leaderboard of a competition -> use get_competition_winners.
- Live standings while a competition is still running -> use get_leaderboard_list / get_leaderboard_top.
- The customer's competition trading ACCOUNTS / credentials / balance -> use get_free_competition_accounts.
- Listing competitions or getting the competition_id -> use get_competitions first.

WHY THIS EXISTS: this is customer-scoped and direct — it reads ONLY the customer's own competition_winners row (joined through a competition account they own), so it answers 'did I win' without scanning the public winners list.

PREREQUISITES: competition_id (REQUIRED). Get it from get_competitions (the 'id' field).

RETURNS: { competition_id, won (bool), participated (bool — true if the customer has a competition account in this competition), result: null when won=false, otherwise { winner_id, competition_account_id, login, position (e.g. '1st','15th'), gain_percentage (float), prize (verbatim string, e.g. '$0.00' or '$5,000'), has_prize (bool — false when prize is $0.00/empty), package, winner_type (1=General,2=Lottery), winner_type_label, certificate_status (tinyint), certificate_available (bool — true when certificate_status=1), status (tinyint), status_label (Draft|Approved|In Progress|Account Disbursed|Account & Payout Disbursed|Rejected), remarks, created_at (ISO8601) } }.

INTERPRETATION:
- won=false, participated=true  -> the customer took part but is not on the winners list (did NOT win).
- won=false, participated=false -> the customer has no account in this competition.
- A winner can be ranked/drawn with no money (prize '$0.00' / has_prize=false) — say they placed/won a slot but received no cash prize; do NOT claim a cash prize when has_prize=false.
- Quote position, gain_percentage and prize VERBATIM. Use winner_type_label and status_label for human phrasing.

ERROR HANDLING:
- 422 -> competition_id missing or not a positive integer. Ask for / re-fetch the competition_id via get_competitions.
- 404 -> authenticated customer could not be resolved.
- 401 -> not authenticated.
- 500 -> backend error; retry once, then escalate.

SECURITY: read-only and strictly customer-scoped — only ever returns the authenticated customer's own winner row.

RELATED KNOWLEDGE — the search_knowledge tool covers the related rules/policies when the customer question touches prize rules, disbursement timing, certificate process, or 'why/how/when'. This tool returns the customer's real RESULT/NUMBERS; the knowledge base holds the RULES (prize distribution, payout timing, certificate issuance) behind them.

competition_id.description: Competition ID (the 'id' field from get_competitions). Required; must be a positive integer.

name: get_account_consistency_status
title: Account Consistency Rule Status
description:
PROACTIVE weekly lot/trade consistency-rule status for ONE trading account — shows where the account stands against the consistency limits BEFORE a breach happens, not just after.

WHEN TO USE:
- 'Am I close to breaking the consistency rule?'
- 'How many lots/trades can I do this week to stay consistent?'
- 'Why did I get a consistency violation last week?'
- 'What are my lot/trade limits this week?'

SCOPE — WHICH ACCOUNTS HAVE THIS RULE: The weekly lot/trade consistency rule ONLY applies to paid Express-plan CFD accounts (Express Demo / Express Real). It does NOT apply to Evaluation, Stellar, Stellar Instant, Flex, Futures, FREE-TRIAL, or COMPETITION accounts — those carry no consistency rule and this tool returns rule_applicable=false, status='not_applicable' for them. account_id here is a PAID account id (from get_accounts / resolve_account); do NOT pass a free-trial or competition account id — that resolves to a different id space and returns 'Account not found'. For a free-trial or competition account, there is no consistency rule to report — answer that directly and do NOT call this tool.

HOW THE RULE WORKS: From week 2 of the subscription onward, each week's per-active-trading-day lot average must stay within [lots_lower_limit, lots_upper_limit] and the per-active-trading-day trade-count average must stay within [trade_lower_limit, trade_upper_limit]. The band is derived from the running average of PRIOR weeks (upper = 2x, lower = 0.5x). Week 1 has no band (rule_applicable=false) because there is no prior-week baseline. An account with no trading activity in the current subscription also returns status='not_applicable'.

READING THE ANSWER: For 'how many more can I do', use current_week.lots.headroom_to_upper and current_week.trades.headroom_to_upper (how much more per-active-day average is still allowed before hitting the upper cap; 0 means already over). buffer_above_lower shows distance above the lower floor. state is within_limits | over_upper_limit | under_lower_limit. pct_of_band is 0 at the lower floor and 100 at the upper cap.

LIVE vs STORED: current_week and weeks[] are computed LIVE from the account's actual trades (matches the dashboard consistency view). stored_violations[] are the historical violation rows recorded in account_consistency_remarks (only weeks that already violated are logged there). NOTE on stored_violations averages: by a legacy upstream storage convention, the stored lot_weekly_average actually holds the recorded TRADE-count average and trade_weekly_average actually holds the recorded LOT average (the two were swapped at write time). They are surfaced verbatim under their stored names to match the admin panel / account overview. When answering a historical 'what was my lot/trade average that week' question, prefer the correctly-labelled LIVE weeks[] values; do not quote the swapped stored_violations averages as the historical lot/trade average.

PREREQUISITES: account_id. If the customer gives a login number, call resolve_account first.

RETURNS: { account{ id, login, is_breached, stored_violation_count }, rule_applicable, status(consistent|violated|not_applicable), message, current_week{ week_number, week_start_date, week_end_date, rule_applies_this_week, total_lots, total_trades, active_trading_days, lot_daily_average, trade_daily_average, lots_upper_limit, lots_lower_limit, trade_upper_limit, trade_lower_limit, lots{current_daily_average,lower_limit,upper_limit,state,headroom_to_upper,buffer_above_lower,pct_of_band}, trades{...}, lots_rule_violated, trades_rule_violated, is_consistent }, weeks[ same shape per started week ], stored_violations[ { id, type, remarks, week_number, week_start_date, week_end_date, total_lots, total_trade, lots_upper_limit, lots_lower_limit, trade_upper_limit, trade_lower_limit, active_trading_day, lot_weekly_average, trade_weekly_average, recorded_at } ] }.

account_id.description: Internal account_id of a PAID Express-plan CFD account (from get_accounts or resolve_account). Do NOT pass a free-trial or competition account id — those have no consistency rule and will return 'Account not found'.

name: get_coupon_redemption_history
title: Coupon Redemption History (Coupons Used + Savings)
description:
Returns which coupons the customer has ALREADY USED on purchases and how much money they saved, newest first and PAGINATED. READ-ONLY.

WHEN TO USE — any 'coupons I have used / money saved' question:
- 'Which coupons have I used?'
- 'How much have I saved with coupons / discount codes?'
- 'What discount did I get on my last purchase?'
- 'How many times did I use the <CODE> coupon?'

WHEN NOT TO USE: for coupons the customer can STILL USE (available/active coupons), use get_user_coupons / get_dynamic_checkout_coupons. For full order/payment history use get_order_history / get_payment_history. This tool is the INVERSE of the available-coupon tools — it reports past redemptions, not usable coupons.

WHY THIS EXISTS: the existing coupon tools only surface coupons that are still usable; none of them answer 'which coupons did I already use and what did they save me'. This reads from the customer's own orders that had a coupon attached (orders.coupon_id), joined to the coupon (name/code) and the purchased plan, with the per-order discount applied.

SCOPE: hard-scoped to the authenticated customer's own orders only. 'Redeemed'/'saved' counts COMPLETED orders only — a coupon attached to a pending or cancelled order is NOT counted as money saved (it carries status_label so the LLM can explain that). By default the paginated list shows completed orders only; set completed_only=false to also list pending/cancelled coupon orders.

PARAMETERS (all optional): page (page number, default 1); per_page (rows per page, 1-50, default 15); completed_only (boolean, default true — when false, the list also includes pending/cancelled coupon-attached orders; summary and by_coupon totals always reflect completed orders only).

RETURNS: { summary{ redeemed_coupon_orders, distinct_coupons_used, total_saved, note }, by_coupon[ { coupon_id, coupon_name, coupon_code, coupon_type (1=flat amount, 2=percentage), coupon_type_label, times_used, total_saved, last_used_at } ] (top coupons by savings, capped at 20), list_scope (completed_only|all_coupon_orders), history{ paginated: current_page, per_page, total, next_page_url, prev_page_url, data[] where each item = { order_id, coupon_id, coupon_name, coupon_code, coupon_type, coupon_type_label, coupon_value, plan, order_total, discount_applied, amount_paid, status, status_label, is_redeemed, order_date } } }. Quote total_saved / discount_applied verbatim.

page.description: Page number to fetch (1-based). Defaults to 1. Walk older redemptions by following history.next_page_url.

per_page.description: Rows per page for the history list, 1-50. Defaults to 15.

completed_only.description: When true (default) the history list shows only completed orders (true redemptions). When false it also lists coupon-attached orders that are pending or cancelled. The summary and by_coupon totals always count completed orders only.

name: get_coupon_reward_share_history
title: Coupon Reward-Share History
description:
Reward-share coupon disbursements the customer has EARNED (cash paid across payout cycles), grouped by coupon, plus the configured reward schedule for their redeemed coupons. Existing coupon tools only show the coupon config, never the disbursed amounts.

WHEN TO USE: 'how much reward share have I earned from my coupon', 'when is my next reward payout', 'how much am I still owed on my reward-share coupon'.

PREREQUISITES: none — scoped to the authenticated customer (via orders.customer_id).

RETURNS: { summary{total_reward_earned, payout_count, distinct_coupons}, by_coupon[...], payouts[...], reward_schedule[...] }.

name: get_free_trial_eligibility
title: Free Trial Eligibility Precheck
description:
READ-ONLY precheck of whether the authenticated customer can create a free-trial account. Use this BEFORE create_free_trial_account so the customer never has to fire the destructive create endpoint just to read back a rejection.

WHEN TO USE — any 'can I / why can't I' free-trial question:
- 'Can I create a free trial?' / 'Why can't I make another one?'
- 'Is the free trial available in my country?'
- 'Do I already have an active trial?'

LOGIC (mirrors the create-path gates, in order): (1) restricted country — if the customer's country is on the restricted list AND no USA-only plan is available to them, the product is not offered; (2) one active trial per customer — if they already hold a free-trial account with status active, they cannot create another; otherwise eligible. Country lists come from the canonical backend helpers (not hardcoded).

PREREQUISITES: none — scoped to the authenticated customer; takes no parameters.

RETURNS: { eligible(bool), reason(string — human-readable; when blocked by an active trial it is verbatim the create endpoint's own message ('You have already an active account!') and when blocked by country it is verbatim the create endpoint's country message), has_active_trial(bool), country_allowed(bool), country_id, is_usa_country(bool), is_restricted_country(bool), active_trial{ account_id, login, plan } | null, available_plans[ { free_trial_plan_id, title, type, starting_balance, duration, is_usa_plan } ], allowed_servers (USA customers only) }.

name: get_free_trial_summary
title: Free Trial Summary (Cross-Trial Rollup)
description:
READ-ONLY cross-trial rollup of EVERY free-trial account the authenticated customer owns. Free trial has no cycle abstraction — each renewal is an independent free-trial account — so no single dashboard surface answers 'all my trials combined' questions. This is that surface.

WHEN TO USE — any lifetime / combined / aggregate free-trial question across the customer's trials:
- 'How have all my trials done combined?'
- 'What is my aggregate win-rate across my trials?'
- 'What is my lifetime trial P&L?'
- 'How many free trials have I had / how many were breached?'

WHAT IT IS NOT: this is a multi-trial ROLLUP, not single-account detail. For one specific trial's trading history use get_free_trial_trading_history / get_free_trial_overview; for whether a NEW trial can be created use get_free_trial_eligibility.

LOGIC: groups free_trial_accounts by the authenticated customer_id, aggregates free_trial_trades per trial in SQL (net_pnl = sum of profit + commission + swap; win_rate = wins over CLOSED trades, where a win is profit >= 0), and joins each trial's latest subscription ending_at. Lifetime totals are computed across ALL the customer's trials, not just the returned page.

PAGINATION: a customer may hold 1000+ trials, so the per-trial list is paginated. Optional `page` (default 1) and `per_page` (default 25, max 100). The `totals` block is always lifetime-wide regardless of page.

PREREQUISITES: none — scoped entirely to the authenticated customer; no account/login id is accepted.

RETURNS: { totals: { trial_count, active_trial_count, breached_trial_count, total_starting_balance, lifetime_net_pnl, total_trade_count, aggregate_win_rate(0-100 over closed trades, or null when none closed) }, trials: [ { account_id, login, status('active'|'inactive'), is_active(bool), breached(bool), starting_balance, net_pnl, trade_count, win_rate(0-100 or null), ending_at(latest subscription end, or null), created_at } ], pagination: { total, current_page, last_page, has_more } }. Numeric fields are null only when the underlying data is absent.

page.description: Page number of the per-trial list (1-based). Optional; defaults to 1.

per_page.description: Trials per page. Optional; defaults to 25, capped at 100. Does not affect the lifetime totals block.

name: get_if_payout_cycle_history
title: InstantFunding Payout-Cycle History (Tier Growth + Splits + Growth-Fund Retention)
description:
Per-cycle InstantFunding / Futures payout history for ONE account, across ALL of its payout cycles, in a single call. For each cycle it returns: the tier the account was on, the % growth earned that cycle, whether the cycle triggered a tier SCALE-UP and whether it was an on-demand payout, how much profit-share was RETAINED to the growth fund, and the PAYOUT SPLIT (amount requested vs amount actually disbursed, with status). It also returns a tier ladder (the progression of tiers reached with cumulative growth per tier) and lifetime totals.

WHEN TO USE:
- 'Show my tier-growth and payout splits over time'
- 'How much was retained to the growth fund each cycle?'
- 'How did my tier grow across cycles / when did I scale up?'
- 'What did I request vs what was actually disbursed each cycle?'
- 'How many times have I scaled up on this account?'

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Forward-looking payout TERMS / caps (profit-split %, payout cadence, max-withdrawal limit) -> use get_account_payout_terms.
- A single pending payout's deduction breakdown -> use get_payout_breakdown_data.
- The customer's general payout REQUEST history / statuses across all account types -> use get_payout_history / get_payout_status.
- Per-cycle TRADING P&L / win-rate -> use account all-cycles summary / get_cycle_overview.

WHY THIS EXISTS: an InstantFunding account grows tier-by-tier; each payout cycle records its tier growth, the profit-share retained to the growth fund, and a payout split, but these live in three separate tables (tier-growths, growth-funds, wallet-transactions) and the dashboard never shows them together over time. This tool stitches them per cycle so the LLM can narrate the account's tier-growth and payout story in one response.

PREREQUISITES: account_id (REQUIRED, integer). If the customer gives a login number, call resolve_account first to convert it. The account must belong to the authenticated customer (ownership enforced server-side; a non-owned id returns 404). This is an InstantFunding/Futures feature — a non-IF account (or an IF account that has never paid out) returns empty cycles / a zeroed summary, not an error.

RETURNS: { account{ id, login, plan, platform(cfd|futures), account_starting_balance(float|null), is_breached(bool) }, summary{ total_cycles(int), disbursed_payout_count(int), starting_tier(int|null), highest_tier_reached(int|null), max_tier(int), scale_up_count(int), on_demand_payout_count(int), total_growth_fund_retained(float), total_payout_requested(float), total_payout_disbursed(float) }, tier_ladder[ { tier(int), total_growth_pct(float), cycles_in_tier(int), scaled_up(bool), first_reached_at(iso8601|null) } ] (oldest tier first), cycles[ { cycle_number(int, 1=oldest), subscription_id(int|null), occurred_at(iso8601|null), starting_balance(float|null), tier_growth{ tier(int), tier_after_cycle(int), growth_pct(float|null), is_scale_up(bool), is_on_demand_payout(bool) }, growth_fund_retained(float|null), payout_split{ requested_amount(float|null), disbursed_amount(float|null), commission_amount(float|null), status(int), status_label(string|null), is_disbursed(bool), note(string|null), requested_at(iso8601|null), approved_at(iso8601|null) }|null } ] (oldest cycle first) }.

INTERPRETATION:
- growth_fund_retained is the profit-share AMOUNT moved to the growth fund for that cycle (the IF model: profit-share is retained to the growth fund and paid out as the split).
- payout_split.requested_amount is what the customer requested; payout_split.disbursed_amount is what was actually paid out — they can differ when a per-payout cap applies (e.g. requested 2480, disbursed 496). Quote BOTH verbatim; do not assume they are equal.
- tier_growth.is_scale_up=true means that cycle's growth pushed the account up a tier; tier_after_cycle shows the tier it scaled to. growth_pct is the percentage growth recorded for that single cycle.
- starting_balance is the account's funded balance for that cycle; it increases each time the account scales up (e.g. 5000 -> 10000 -> 15000 ...).
- summary.highest_tier_reached vs summary.max_tier shows how far the account climbed against the program ceiling.
- payout_split=null means a cycle's tier-growth row had no matching payout transaction (rare); growth_fund_retained may still be present.
- A null field means the underlying value is absent — never substitute 0 for null. Quote all amounts, tiers, percentages and counts VERBATIM; never invent fields or values.

PRIVACY: only customer-safe payout notes (public_remark) are returned; internal ops remarks are never exposed.

ERROR HANDLING:
- 404 'Account not found.' -> the account_id is not owned by this customer (or does not exist); re-resolve the login.
- 422 -> account_id missing or non-integer.
- 500 -> transient backend error; retry once, then advise support.

⚠️ RELATED KNOWLEDGE — the search_knowledge tool covers the related rules/policies whenever the question touches HOW tier growth, scale-ups, growth-fund retention, or payout splits WORK (rules / eligibility / thresholds / timing). This tool returns the customer's real per-cycle NUMBERS; the knowledge base holds the policy RULES behind them (and is the source of truth for policy). It supplies the policy context behind the numbers.

name: get_kyc_account_overview
title: KYC Account Overview
description:
A PER-ACCOUNT KYC (identity verification) roll-up for the authenticated customer: which of the customer's accounts are KYC-approved, which still need action. Groups the customer's own customer_kycs rows by account and reports each account's verification state in a single call, with NO platform_id and NO account_id required.

WHEN TO USE — any 'across my accounts' KYC question:
- 'Which of my accounts is KYC-approved?'
- 'What's my KYC status across all my accounts?'
- 'Are all my accounts verified, or only some?'
- 'Which accounts still need KYC / still need action?'

WHEN NOT TO USE: for the customer's SINGLE latest KYC decision/state (am I verified, is my latest attempt done) use get_kyc_current_status; for the reason behind a failed/returned attempt use get_kyc_latest_decision_reason; the older get_kyc_status requires a Veriff platform_id customers never have.

WHY THIS EXISTS: get_kyc_current_status reports the single latest decision; this tool answers the account-by-account question by grouping KYC sessions per account.

HOW is_verified IS DECIDED (per account): true only when that account currently holds an ACTIVE approved KYC (status='approved' AND approval_status=1). An account that was approved before but whose active approval is gone (e.g. expired/abandoned/replaced) returns is_verified=false with verification_state='reverification_required' and has_ever_approved=true. Per-account is_verified is NOT the same as the customer-wide payout-gate recency in `renewal`.

PREREQUISITES: None — uses the authenticated customer (Sanctum bearer). No login, account_id, or platform_id needed. A customer can NEVER see another customer's accounts or KYC.

RETURNS: { has_kyc(bool), total_accounts_with_kyc(int), verified_account_count(int), ever_approved_account_count(int), action_required_account_count(int), renewal{ enforced(bool), kyc_required(bool), re_verify(bool), days_left(int, or null when enforced=false), last_approved_at(datetime|null), message(string|null) }, accounts[ { account_id(int), login(customer-facing account login string/number, or null if not resolvable), is_verified(bool), verification_state(verified|reverification_required|under_review|resubmission_requested|declined|expired|abandoned|in_progress|not_started), latest_status(raw latest meaningful status string or null: approved|resubmission_requested|declined|abandoned|expired|rejected|under_review), latest_status_label, platform_name(veriff|sumsub|null), has_ever_approved(bool), action_required(bool), last_session_at(datetime|null), session_count(int) } ], summary(string) }.

RENEWAL POLICY: renewal.enforced=false means the periodic KYC renewal is switched off platform-wide (since 2026-09-18): an APPROVED KYC does not expire, days_left is null, and the customer does NOT need to re-verify. In that case never tell the customer they must renew or re-verify after 90 days, even if the knowledge base still describes a 'Mandatory 90-Day KYC Renewal' (that article predates the change). renewal.enforced=true means days_left is real.

INTERPRETATION:
- Only accounts with at least one meaningful KYC session appear in `accounts`; an account with no KYC activity is not listed (total_accounts_with_kyc counts only listed accounts).
- Identify a verified account to the customer by its `login` (the number they recognise), not the internal account_id.
- action_required=true means that account's latest KYC was declined/rejected/resubmission_requested/expired/abandoned and it is not currently verified.
- `renewal` is customer-wide payout-gate recency (the same truth the dashboard uses), NOT per account.

ACCURACY: Quote logins, statuses, counts, and dates VERBATIM. Never invent an account, status, or count not present in the response. If `accounts` is empty, say no account-level KYC sessions were found.

⚠️ RELATED KNOWLEDGE — the search_knowledge tool covers the related rules/policies when the question touches any rule/policy/process (e.g. whether KYC is per-account or per-customer, KYC requirements for payout, how many accounts need KYC). This tool returns the customer's real per-account STATE; the knowledge base holds the RULES and is the source of truth for policy.

name: get_account_payout_terms
title: Account Payout Terms & Withdrawal Caps
description:
Per-account FORWARD-LOOKING payout terms + withdrawal-cap readiness in a single call: the profit-split % the customer keeps, how often they can be paid (weekly / bi-weekly), and the caps that limit a withdrawal (per-payout cap, per-cycle max-withdrawal limit, payout buffer, max number of payouts) together with how many payouts have already been disbursed.

WHEN TO USE:
- 'What % of profit do I keep on this account?'
- 'How often can I get paid / what's my payout cycle?'
- 'When is my first / next payout window?'
- 'Which payout option is my account on?'
- 'Why can't I withdraw the full amount?'
- 'How many payouts do I have left on this account?'
- 'What's the maximum I can withdraw per payout / per cycle?'

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- The customer's actual payout REQUEST history (amounts, dates, statuses) -> use get_payout_history / get_payout_status.
- The breakdown of a specific pending payout amount -> use get_payout_breakdown_data.
- Current-cycle trading P&L / balance -> use get_cycle_overview / get_account_balance.

WHY THIS EXISTS: the dashboard scatters profit-split, payout cadence and the withdrawal caps across several screens. This tool resolves them all from the account's effective rules (plan defaults merged with per-account overrides) and pairs them with realised disbursement consumption so the LLM can explain payout terms and why a balance is not fully withdrawable in one call.

TERMS SOURCE: profit-split (PS), weekly (AWP) / bi-weekly (BWP) payout, payout cap (FPC), payout buffer (PBA), max-withdrawal limit (MWL), max-payout-count (MWPC) and final-payout amount (FPA) are read from the account's effective rule set. Any rule NOT configured for the account is returned as null — never assume a default.

CAP SEMANTICS (important when explaining 'why can't I withdraw the full amount'):
- payout_cap (FPC) caps a SINGLE payout, not a lifetime total.
- max_withdrawal_limit (MWL) caps the withdrawal per cycle.
- max_payout_count (MWPC) caps the TOTAL number of payouts the account may ever receive; cap_consumption.payouts_made (count of DISBURSED payouts) vs payouts_remaining shows how many are left.
- payout_buffer_amount (PBA) is the buffer that must remain above starting balance before a payout is released.
- final_payout_amount (FPA) caps the last payout once the payout count is reached.
- cap_consumption.why_capped is a ready-made list of the caps that actually apply to this account (omitted entries simply do not apply).

PREREQUISITES: account_id (REQUIRED, integer). If the customer gives a login number, call resolve_account first to convert it. The account must belong to the authenticated customer (ownership enforced server-side; a non-owned id returns 404).

RETURNS: { account{ id, login, plan, platform(cfd|futures) }, profit_split{ percentage(float|null), source(account_override|plan_default|null) }, payout_cycle{ frequency(weekly|bi_weekly|null), weekly_enabled(bool|null), bi_weekly_enabled(bool|null) }, payout_option{ id(int), label(string|null), payout_flow(scheduled_cycle|on_request_once_eligible), cycle_days(int|null), first_cycle_days(int|null), current_cycle_ends_at('Y-m-d H:i:s'|null), min_profitable_days(int|null), growth_percentage(float|null), consistency_percentage(int|null), applies_to(this_funded_account|funded_account_after_challenge) } | null, withdrawal_caps{ payout_cap(float|null), max_withdrawal_limit(float|null), payout_buffer_amount(float|null), max_payout_count(int|null), final_payout_amount(float|null) }, cap_consumption{ payouts_made(int), max_payout_count(int|null), payouts_remaining(int|null), total_disbursed(float), per_payout_cap(float|null), why_capped(string[]|null) } }.

INTERPRETATION:
- frequency=null means no weekly/bi-weekly override is set on the account (standard cadence) — do NOT claim weekly or bi-weekly.
- weekly_enabled (AWP) and bi_weekly_enabled (BWP) are independent ON/OFF flags with NO day count; never derive a number of days from them. The only day counts are in payout_option. If both flags are true, frequency reports 'weekly' (the more frequent cadence) but both raw flags are still returned.
- payout_option is the Stellar payout option stamped on this account. When present it IS the account's payout schedule and overrides the knowledge base's generic plan schedule: Stellar Lite accounts bought or reset from 12 Oct 2026 run on 'Stellar Lite Modified' (10-day cycles, no 21-day first cycle), while older accounts on the same plan keep the legacy schedule. payout_option=null means no option is stamped; the plan's standard schedule applies.
- For the date of the next payout window, quote current_cycle_ends_at verbatim. Never compute it from cycle_days: Stellar Lite Modified cycles count weekdays and close at 23:45.
- payout_flow=on_request_once_eligible (3 Day / On-Demand options) has no fixed cycle: the customer requests a payout once the gates in min_profitable_days / growth_percentage / consistency_percentage are met.
- A null cap means that cap is not configured for the account; say it is 'not capped' rather than reporting 0.
- Quote percentage, caps, total_disbursed and counts VERBATIM — never round or invent values.

ERROR HANDLING:
- 404 'Account not found.' -> the account_id is not owned by this customer (or does not exist); re-resolve the login.
- 422 -> account_id missing or non-integer.
- 500 -> transient backend error; retry once, then advise support.

⚠️ RELATED KNOWLEDGE — the search_knowledge tool covers the related rules/policies whenever the question touches payout rules/policy/eligibility/timing/fees or asks 'why'/'how'/'can I'. This tool returns the customer's real account TERMS and NUMBERS; the knowledge base holds the policy RULES behind them (and is the source of truth for policy). It supplies the policy context behind the numbers.

name: get_customer_portfolio_rollup
title: Cross-Account Portfolio Rollup
description:
Cross-account portfolio rollup so 'how am I doing overall?' is answerable in ONE call. Returns a PAGINATED list of ALL the customer's trading accounts — each with current balance, lifetime net P&L, trade count, win rate and breached flag — plus customer-wide totals. READ-ONLY.

WHEN TO USE — any portfolio-level / cross-account question:
- 'How am I doing across all my accounts?'
- 'What is my total lifetime P&L across every account?'
- 'Which account performs best?'
- 'How many of my accounts have I breached?'
- 'How many accounts do I have in total?'

WHEN NOT TO USE: for ONE account's detail use get_account_overview / get_trading_overview; for one account's all-cycle history use get_account_all_cycles_summary; to convert a login number to an account use resolve_account.

WHY THIS EXISTS: the per-account tools answer one account at a time, so a portfolio view would need one call per account. This rolls every account up in a single paginated call.

P&L NOTE: lifetime_net_pnl per account is the sum of that account's closed-trade net P&L. For CFD (MT5) accounts it is profit + commission + swap from the trades table; for Futures (Tradovate) accounts it is net_pnl from the futures_trades table (no swap). Platform is detected per account, so mixed portfolios are correct. Values are lifetime across all of the account's resets/cycles.

PERFORMANCE: a customer may own 1000+ accounts, so the account list is PAGINATED (per_page capped at 50, default 25). page_net_pnl, page_trade_count and best_account_on_page are scoped to the CURRENT PAGE only; total_accounts and breached_account_count in totals span the WHOLE portfolio. To find the single best account across a large portfolio, sort the customer's accounts by lifetime_net_pnl across pages.

PARAMETERS (all optional): page (page number, 1-based, default 1); per_page (accounts per page, 1-50, default 25).

RETURNS: { current_page, per_page, last_page, total, next_page_url, prev_page_url, data[ per-account { account_id, login, plan, platform(cfd|futures), status(active|breached), under_review, current_balance, starting_balance, lifetime_net_pnl, trade_count, win_rate, breached, breach_event_count } ], totals{ total_accounts, breached_account_count }, page_summary{ accounts_on_page, page_net_pnl, page_trade_count, best_account_on_page{ account_id, login, plan, lifetime_net_pnl }, note } }.

title: FN002 Transfer-Payout Preview & Eligibility
description:
For a FundedNext FN002 (step) real account, previews how much the customer would ACTUALLY receive if they transferred their payout right now, and whether they are eligible — in one call.

WHEN TO USE:
- 'How much will I get if I take my payout on this FN002 account?'
- 'What's my profit share / net payout right now?'
- 'Am I eligible to transfer my payout?'
- 'Why can't I transfer my payout?' (returns the exact blocking reason)

- CFD-Flex payout preview -> use get_cfd_flex_payout_preview.
- The breakdown of an already-requested/pending payout -> use get_payout_breakdown_data.
- The customer's payout REQUEST history (amounts, dates, statuses) -> use get_payout_history / get_payout_status.
- Forward-looking payout caps / profit-split terms -> use get_account_payout_terms.

WHY THIS EXISTS: transfer payout is an FN002-only flow. This tool runs the same eligibility + breakdown calculation the dashboard uses, but returns clean numbers (the dashboard bakes them into an HTML string) and, instead of failing on an ineligible account, tells you WHY it is blocked.

PREREQUISITES: account_id (REQUIRED, integer). If the customer gives a login number, call resolve_account first. The account must belong to the authenticated customer (ownership enforced server-side; a non-owned id returns 404).

RETURNS: { account{ id, login, plan }, applicable(bool), eligible(bool), ineligible_reason(string|null), breakdown{ total_profit(float), news_trade_deduction(float), risk_deduction(float), net_amount(float), profit_share(float) }|null }.

INTERPRETATION:
- applicable=false -> this is NOT an FN002 account; transfer payout does not apply (ineligible_reason says so). Do not attempt a breakdown.
- eligible=true -> breakdown is populated; profit_share is the amount the customer would receive (net_amount x profit-split %). Quote total_profit, news_trade_deduction, risk_deduction, net_amount and profit_share VERBATIM.
- eligible=false with applicable=true -> the account IS FN002 but a rule blocks a transfer right now; ineligible_reason holds the exact cause (e.g. open trades, not in profit, active trading day, minimum profitable days not met). Relay that reason. breakdown is null.
- Never round or invent figures; null caps/values mean not-configured, not zero.

- 404 'Account not found.' -> account_id not owned by this customer (or does not exist); re-resolve the login.
- 422 -> account_id missing or non-integer.
- 500 -> transient backend error; retry once, then advise support.

⚠️ RELATED KNOWLEDGE — call search_knowledge whenever the question touches payout RULES/policy/eligibility/timing/fees or asks 'why'/'how'/'can I'. This tool returns the customer's real NUMBERS and current eligibility; the knowledge base holds the transfer-payout POLICY behind them (and is the source of truth on policy).

name: get_trusted_devices
title: Trusted / Logged-in Devices
description:

- 'Which device am I using right now?'

WHAT IT RETURNS: one row per trusted device for the authenticated customer, most-recently-used first. name: get_wrap_by_year
title: FN Wrap (Year-in-Review) for Any Year
description:
FN Wrap year-in-review for ANY supported calendar year, plus a catalogue of which years the customer has a wrap for. The dashboard wrap is locked to last calendar year only; this tool computes the SAME wrap figures for a real, caller-supplied year (2022 onward) so the customer can revisit, e.g., their 2023 or 2024 wrap.

TWO MODES (one endpoint):
1) NO account_id -> 'eligible-years' catalogue: every year (2022+) for which the customer has a wrap-eligible account, with the eligible account_ids/logins and per-year trade counts under each year. Use for 'Which years do I have a wrap for?'.
2) account_id (+ optional year) -> the wrap OVERVIEW for that one owned account and year. If `year` is omitted it defaults to the previous calendar year (clamped to the 2022 wrap floor).

WHEN TO USE:
- 'Show my 2023 wrap' / 'Show my 2024 year-in-review' -> pass account_id + year.
- 'Which years do I have a wrap for?' / 'List my wrap years' -> call with NO account_id.
- 'My best trade / most-traded pair / total lots in 2023' -> account_id + year=2023.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- Current open positions or live balance -> use get_account_balance / get_cycle_overview.
- All-cycle lifetime account stats (not calendar-year scoped) -> use the all-cycles summary tool.
- Generating or sharing a NEW wrap share link -> this tool is READ-ONLY and only returns an EXISTING share code if one was already created on the dashboard.

WHY THIS EXISTS: the production wrap service hardcodes 'previous year' in every query, so older wraps are unreachable. This tool re-runs the identical wrap aggregation for the requested year and reuses the canonical wrap trading-math (lots, average RRR, best trade, total trades) so the numbers match the dashboard wrap exactly — only the YEAR differs.

ELIGIBILITY: a wrap needs BOTH (a) at least 10 closed trades in that year (`has_min_trades`) AND (b) a wrap-eligible breach state — not breached, or breached only by 'Profit Target Reached' (`breach_state_eligible`). `is_eligible` is the AND of both; when false the overview still returns whatever data exists for transparency, and the two sub-flags say which gate failed.

PREREQUISITES: For mode 2, account_id (integer) must belong to the authenticated customer (ownership enforced server-side; a non-owned id returns 404). If the customer gives a login number, call resolve_account first. `year` must be 2022..current year.

RETURNS (mode 1, no account_id): { min_wrap_year(int), default_year(int), min_trades_for_wrap(int), years: [ { year(int), eligible_account_count(int), accounts: [ { account_id(int), login, trade_count(int) } ] } ] (newest year first) }.
RETURNS (mode 2, account_id): { account{ id, login, plan }, year(int), is_eligible(bool), has_min_trades(bool), breach_state_eligible(bool), min_trades_for_wrap(int), overview{ type, starting_balance(float|null), most_trade_pair(string|null), lots(float), average_rrr(string|null e.g. '1:2.4'), total_trades(int), best_trade(float), best_trade_date(string|null), payout_amount(float, that year's disbursements), trader_type('Elite Trader'|'Crown Trader'|null) }, share{ code(string|null), is_shared(bool) } }.

INTERPRETATION:
- average_rrr is a ratio string like '1:2.4'; null when there were no losing trades to ratio against. Do not invent a number.
- most_trade_pair / trader_type / best_trade_date / starting_balance can be null when absent — say 'not available', never fabricate.
- payout_amount is the disbursed payout total for THAT year on that account, not lifetime.
- share.code is null unless the customer already generated a wrap share link; this tool never creates one.
- Quote year, lots, best_trade, payout_amount, trade_count and counts VERBATIM.

ERROR HANDLING:
- 404 'Account not found.' -> the account_id is not owned by this customer (or does not exist); re-resolve the login.
- 422 -> year out of range (must be 2022..current) or non-integer account_id/year.
- 500 -> transient backend error; retry once, then advise support.

⚠️ RELATED KNOWLEDGE — the search_knowledge tool covers the related rules/policies when the question touches what FN Wrap is, eligibility rules, or 'why isn't there a wrap for X'. This tool returns the customer's real wrap NUMBERS; the knowledge base holds the wrap RULES/policy behind them.

account_id.description: Internal account_id of the trading account whose wrap you want. OMIT this to instead list every year the customer has a wrap for. Use resolve_account to convert a login number to an account_id first.

year.description: Calendar year of the wrap (2022..current year). Only used with account_id. Defaults to the previous calendar year when omitted.

title: Get Payout Status
description:
Enum of all possible payout status codes + labels for filter dropdowns. Reference lookup.

WHEN TO USE: Rare — primarily for populating a status filter UI, or when you need the canonical code → label mapping to translate a status returned by another tool. Most AI sessions won't need this since status codes are documented in get_payout_history response_labels.

RETURNS: enum mapping object — { code (int) → label (string) }.
FULL STATUS CODE TABLE (CUSTOMER-FACING TRANSLATIONS):
- 1  → 'Approved' (admin approved, awaiting disbursement)
- 2  → 'Rejected' (admin rejected — customer should request review)
- 3  → 'Not Requested Yet' (no payout request submitted)
- 4  → 'Under Review' (admin reviewing payout request)
- 5  → 'Hold' (payout on hold — usually KYC or compliance check)
- 7  → 'Method Confirmation' (waiting for customer to confirm payout method)
- 8  → 'Disbursed' (✅ money sent to customer)
- 9  → 'Not Eligible Yet' (customer hasn't met payout eligibility criteria)
- 10 → 'Request Submitted' (customer submitted, awaiting admin review)
- 11 → 'Additional Due Diligence' (extra checks needed — usually large amounts)
- 12 → 'Ready For Disburse' (queued for disbursement batch)
- 13 → 'Auto Payout Cancelled' (scheduled auto-payout was cancelled)
(Code 6 is reserved/unused)

CUSTOMER PRESENTATION:
- Codes 1, 8, 12 → positive language ('Your payout is approved/disbursed')
- Codes 4, 5, 10, 11 → reassuring ('Your request is being processed')
- Code 2 → empathetic ('Your payout was rejected — let me help you understand why')
- Code 9 → educational ('You need to meet X criteria first')

ERROR HANDLING:
- 401 → not authenticated; re-login.
- 429 → rate-limited; back off.

- gross_profit / gross_loss → "total profits" / "total losses"
- best_trade / worst_trade → "your best trade" / "your worst trade"
- total_commission + total_swap → "trading costs"
- breach → always say "account breach" not technical field names

PROACTIVE COACHING (always include for cycle analysis):
- If profit_factor < 1.0: "⚠️ You're losing more than you're earning — even a good win rate can't overcome a bad risk/reward"
- If |avg_losing_trade| > avg_winning_trade: "⚠️ Your average loss ($X) is bigger than your average win ($Y) — tighten your stop losses or increase your take-profit targets"
- If win_rate > 60% but profit_loss < 0: "You won more trades than you lost, but losses were larger — classic risk/reward problem"
- If total_trading_days < 10 (challenge accounts): "⚠️ Low trading day count — check your plan's minimum requirement with 'how many trading days do I need?'"
- If max_drawdown_pct > 7: "⚠️ You were down more than 7% from your peak — close to most plan limits
MULTI-CYCLE COMPARISON PATTERN:
1. get_account_cycles → all cycle IDs
2. Call get_cycle_overview in parallel for each cycle the customer cares about
3. Compare: profit_loss_pct trend, win_rate trend, profit_factor, max_drawdown_pct
4. For any failed cycle (profit_loss < 0 + is_current = false): call get_rule_breach_history → what rule caused the breach and when
5. Synthesize: 'Across your last 3 cycles, win rate improved (42% → 55% → 61%) but avg losing trade grew — you're winning more but cutting losses slower'


RULE VIOLATIONS PER CYCLE (funded/Real accounts):
- 'What rule did I break in cycle 3?' → get_risk_parameters(account_id, cycle_id=<cycle3 id>) in parallel with this
- cycle_id in get_risk_parameters filters to that cycle's trades only
- Shows: quick_strike %, margin_usage %, news trade deductions, microscalping count for that specific cycle

TRADING DAYS REQUIREMENT:
- total_trading_days here = ACTUAL days traded in this cycle
- Plan MINIMUM required days → call get_account_overview → objectives.trading_days.target_value
- Only applies to challenge accounts (Evaluation/Express plan types); funded/Stellar Instant have no minimum
BREACH CORRELATION: profit_loss < 0 AND is_current = false → also call get_rule_breach_history. Cross-reference breach date with balance_curve to show exactly when the drawdown began.

ERROR HANDLING:
- 401 Unauthenticated → invalid session/token; ask customer to re-login.
- 422 Validation failed → account_id or cycle_id missing/non-integer. Resolve both first.
- 404 Account not found → account_id not owned by this customer; re-run get_accounts / resolve_account.
- 404 Cycle not found → cycle_id doesn't belong to this account; re-run get_account_cycles for a valid cycle_id.
- 500 Internal server error → backend issue; offer to escalate.

⚠️ RELATED KNOWLEDGE — the search_knowledge tool covers the related rules/policies when the customer question touches any rule/policy/process/eligibility/timing/fee or asks 'why'/'how'/'can I'. This tool returns the customer's real NUMBERS/STATE; the knowledge base holds the RULES behind them (and is the source of truth for policy). It supplies the policy context behind the numbers.

FUTURES ACCOUNTS: All trade-level stats (win_rate, profit_factor, gross_profit, gross_loss, best_trade, worst_trade, total_commission) are sourced from `futures_trades` table (Tradovate daily sync) using net_pnl. Balance-curve stats stay sourced from AccountMetric. total_swap is always 0 for Futures (no overnight swap on Futures contracts).

account_id.description: Internal account ID. Customer only knows their login number — call resolve_account(login) first to get this value.

name: get_trading_calendar_month
title: Trading Calendar (Month)
description:
A calendar-grid view of ONE trading account's month: every calendar day of the requested month with its aggregated trading result (net P&L, win rate, trade count) plus a small preview of up to 3 trades. Days with no trades are still returned (has_trade=false). Works for both CFD (MT4/MT5) and Futures accounts.

WHEN TO USE: 'show my calendar for August', 'which days did I trade last month', 'what were my daily results this month', 'my monthly trading heatmap/overview'.

PREREQUISITES: account_id (use resolve_account for a login number first); month in YYYY-MM format (e.g. 2026-08).

RETURNS: { account_id, month, days[ { date, is_weekend, has_trade, has_news, net_pnl, win_rate, total_trades, trades_preview[ {ticket, symbol, type, pnl} ] } ] }.

account_id.description: Internal account_id (resolve a login number via resolve_account first).

month.description: Target month in YYYY-MM format, e.g. "2026-08". Required.

name: get_trading_calendar_day
title: Trading Calendar (Day)
description:
The full trade-by-trade breakdown of ONE trading account on ONE calendar day: a day summary (total trades, win rate, total profit) plus every closed trade with entry/exit prices, times, lots, P&L, P&L %, swap, commission, SL/TP and news flag. Works for both CFD (MT4/MT5) and Futures accounts (Futures rows add gross_pnl and a Micro/Mini volume_type).

WHEN TO USE: 'what did I trade on Aug 15', 'show every trade for that day', 'break down my trades on a specific date', drilling into a single day surfaced by get_trading_calendar_month.

PREREQUISITES: account_id (use resolve_account for a login number first); date in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2026-08-15).

RETURNS: { account_id, date, summary{total_trades, win_rate, total_profit}, trades[ {ticket, symbol, type, lots, has_news, pnl, pnl_percentage, open_price, open_time, close_price, close_time, swap, commission, sl, tp, volume, reason, volume_type} ] }.

account_id.description: Internal account_id (resolve a login number via resolve_account first).

date.description: Target day in YYYY-MM-DD format, e.g. "2026-08-15". Required.

name: get_running_trades
title: Get Running Trades
description:
LIVE open positions on one CFD account right now — every currently-running trade with symbol, lots, open price, SL/TP, commission, and REAL-TIME floating profit/loss (live P&L from the price feed, not a stale snapshot).

WHEN TO USE: 'what trades do I have open right now', 'my open positions', 'am I in any trades', 'current floating P&L', 'running trades'.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- CLOSED trade history → use get_trading_history / get_journal_trades.
- Competition account open trades → use get_competition_running_trades.
- Futures accounts → returns an empty list by design (live futures positions are not served here); say open-position data for Futures is on the trading platform.

PREREQUISITES: account_id (internal id — resolve from login via resolve_account, or from get_accounts).

RETURNS: { trades: PAGINATED [ { ticket, symbol, lots, open_price, sl, tp, commission, profit (LIVE floating P&L — may carry an '(OLD)' suffix when the live feed has no fresh tick), open_time_str, close_time_str: 'Currently Running' } ] }. Empty trades array = no open positions right now (that IS the answer — say so).

ERROR HANDLING: 422 = missing/invalid account_id. Empty for Futures accounts by design.

account_id.description: Internal account id (NOT the login number) — resolve via resolve_account or get_accounts.

cycle_id.description: Optional trading-cycle id to scope stats.

name: get_utility_categories
title: Get Utility Categories
description:
Lightweight list of the category groups used to organize utility items (e.g. Calculators, Risk Management, Education, Account Tools). Returns category metadata only — no items.

WHEN TO USE: Rarely on its own. Only when you need just the category nav labels without the items under them. Customer phrases: 'utility categories', 'what sections are in tools'.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- You want the items AND their categories in one response (the normal case) -> use get_utility_item_category instead.
- You want all items grouped under their category names -> use get_utility_items instead.

PREREQUISITES: None. Public, no IDs required.

RETURNS: { utility_categories: [ { id, name } ] } — active categories only (status=1), ordered by order_value ascending.

ERROR HANDLING: 404 'No category data found' if no active categories exist. 500 'Internal server error' on backend failure — retry once, then escalate.

name: get_utility_items
title: Get Utility Items
description:
All active utility items grouped by their category NAME (educational links, calculators, downloadable tools, account utilities). Cached 1 hour.

WHEN TO USE: 'utility tools', 'what tools are available', 'trading tools', 'list the calculators'. Use when you want items presented grouped under human-readable category titles.

WHEN NOT TO USE: You also need the standalone category list / order metadata in the same call -> use get_utility_item_category instead (returns items keyed by category_id PLUS a separate utility_categories array).

PREREQUISITES: None. Public, no IDs required.

RETURNS: { utility_items: { '<category name>': [ items ], ... } }. The wrapper object 'utility_items' is a dict keyed by the category's display name; each value is an array of item objects (active items only, ordered by order_value ascending). Iterate the keys to render per-category. Cached 1 hour. Example: { utility_items: { 'Reset & Topup': [ { id, name, ... } ], 'Account Tools': [ ... ] } }.

ERROR HANDLING: 404 'No items data found' if no active items exist. 500 'Internal server error' on backend failure — retry once, then escalate.

name: get_utility_item_category
title: Get Utility Item Category
description:
Combined response: active utility items AND the category list in a single call. Cached 30 min. PREFERRED for any utilities-related ask because it avoids two round-trips.

WHEN TO USE: Default for any 'what utility tools / calculators / resources are available' question.

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- You need items already grouped under human-readable category NAMES (not numeric category_id keys) -> use get_utility_items instead.
- You only need the bare category nav labels -> use get_utility_categories instead.

PREREQUISITES: None. Public, no IDs required.

RETURNS: { utility_items: { '<category_id>': [ items ], ... }, utility_categories: [ { id, name } ] }. NOTE the keying difference from get_utility_items: here utility_items is keyed by numeric category_id, and you map each id to a name using the parallel utility_categories array (matched on id). Active items only, ordered by order_value. Cached 30 min.

ERROR HANDLING: 500 'Internal server error' on backend failure — retry once, then escalate. (Empty catalog returns empty collections rather than 404.)

name: get_news_calendar
title: Get News Calendar
description:
Economic / forex news calendar — the CURRENT trading week's economic events (NFP, CPI, rate decisions, etc.) with country, impact level, date and the customer's local time. Source: forexfactory feed (faireconomy), refreshed/cached weekly.

WHEN TO USE: 'economic calendar', 'news events this week', 'what news is coming', 'high-impact news', 'is there NFP this week', 'red-folder news', 'when is CPI'. Pairs with news-trading rule questions (search_knowledge provides the rule).

WHEN NOT TO USE:
- The customer's own news-trade ALERT config / settings -> use get_news_alert_info.
- Per-account news-trade deductions on a payout -> use get_payout_breakdown_data.
- News across an arbitrary date range (admin/extended) -> not exposed here; this tool is current-week only.

PREREQUISITES: timezone is REQUIRED and must be an IANA 'Region/City' string (e.g. 'Asia/Dhaka', 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London') so event times render in the customer's local time. If unknown, ask the customer or derive from get_profile / get_timezone_list.

RETURNS: { getLastWeekData: [ events ], getUniqueCountry: [ country codes ] }. Each event object: { id, title, country, impact (High/Medium/Low), date (formatted 'Do MMM, hh:mm A' in the requested timezone), day (weekday name), timestamp (unix in requested tz), is_restricted (1 if High-impact/restricted), restriction ('Restrictions' | 'No Restrictions'), forecast, previous }. Scoped to the current trading week (Sun–Sat).

CUSTOMER PRESENTATION: group by day; flag high-impact / restricted events; show times in the customer's timezone.

ERROR HANDLING: 422 'Invalid input' if timezone is missing or not in 'Region/City' format (validation errors in data) — re-ask for a valid IANA timezone. Empty week returns empty getLastWeekData (not an error).

This tool returns the customer's real NUMBERS/STATE; the knowledge base holds the RULES behind them (and is the source of truth for policy). It supplies the policy context behind the numbers.

timezone.description: REQUIRED IANA timezone string in 'Region/City' form (e.g. 'Asia/Dhaka', 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London'). Event times are converted to this timezone. Must match the Region/City pattern or the call returns 422.

name: get_platform_download_guide
title: Platform Download Guide

Trading-platform download links and login guide for a given server. name: get_week_wise_news_calendar
title: Week-wise News Calendar
description:
This week's economic news calendar as a 7-day skeleton (Sunday through Saturday), each day carrying its news events grouped under it with impact level, country, and local time. Times are converted to the project timezone. Defaults to the current week; an explicit start_date + end_date custom range can be passed (both required together to activate the range).

RETURNS: { week: [ {date, day, day_short, is_today, news:[ {id,title,time,timestamp,impact,country,date} ]} ] } — one entry per day, Sun→Sat.
